correctness.rationale: For output leaf x at depth k, its signed Haar kernel is constant on each first-divergence sibling subtree, with mass 2^(-j-1), and on x with mass 2^(-k). The signed total variation reduces exactly to sum_{j<k}(1-sigma_j z_j)/2+|z_k|, where z_0=1 and z_{j+1}=(z_j+sigma_j)/2. The Bellman recursion V_m=a_m+c_m|z| has c_m=(1-c_{m-1})/2 and yields F_k. Thus all other branches cancel by mass conservation. Maximum row norm is F_H, attained by choosing the input sign of the kernel. F_{h+1}>F_h for h>=1, and full-binary leaf-count/height inequalities plus successive off-spine leaf splits realize every permissible h; H=N-1 forces a comb. The N=1,2 boundary and maximizing row signs are consistent. Independently enumerated all ordered proper binary trees with <=6 leaves: 65 trees and 351 leaf rows, checking the depth values and height sets. The finite check corroborates but does not prove the unrestricted statement.
